technology_to_test: Autonomous LiDAR drone & wireless relay mesh in dark lava caves
why_suitable: Features natural basaltic lava tube systems with skylight entrances and dark corridors analogous to lunar and Martian pit craters.
analogy_limitations: Earth gravity (1g) is ~6x higher than the Moon; cave interiors contain convective air, mild humidity, and lack sharp electrostatic regolith dust.

technology_to_test: Biosignature sensors, dry-soil drill & perchlorate salt filtration
why_suitable: Hyper-arid core of the Atacama Desert with oxidized salt-rich soils and intense UV radiation closely matching Martian surface conditions.
analogy_limitations: Mean temperature is significantly warmer than Mars (-63°C) and the Moon; 1 atm air pressure and 1g gravity differ from target environments.

technology_to_test: Polar rover suspension, GPS-denied navigation & permafrost drilling
why_suitable: Ancient polar impact crater with cold, fractured rocky terrain analogous to lunar polar regions and Martian impact craters.
analogy_limitations: Retains Earth diurnal cycles, 1 atm atmosphere, and moist snow winds rather than lunar vacuum or tenuous Martian CO2.

technology_to_test: Cryogenic ice-drilling hardware & hypersaline brine detection sensors
why_suitable: Extremely cold, hyper-arid McMurdo Dry Valleys site containing unfrozen hypersaline brines at sub-zero temperatures.
analogy_limitations: Solar elevation and 1 atm air composition differ completely from lunar vacuum; 1g gravity alters material lifting loads.

technology_to_test: Rover mobility trials on loose basaltic slopes & compliant metal wheels
why_suitable: Basaltic lava flow terrain with moderate slopes and loose volcanic cinder dust ideal for Artemis/Mars wheel-slip testing.
analogy_limitations: 1 atm atmosphere and temperate climate do not replicate lunar day-night thermal shocks exceeding 180°C.

technology_to_test: Lava-tube exploration robots & radiation-shielding habitat structures
why_suitable: Large high-altitude basaltic lava tube complex with minimal vegetation, well suited for testing subterranean habitat deployment.
analogy_limitations: High atmospheric humidity and 1g gravity alter ceiling collapse thresholds and structural load behavior compared to 0.16g on the Moon.

technology_to_test: Dry cryogenic permafrost drilling without sample melting
why_suitable: One of the coldest, driest places on Earth with ice-cemented subsurface sand and gravel (dry permafrost).
analogy_limitations: Mean temperature (-23.8°C) remains warmer than the Lunar South Pole (-118°C) and lacks vacuum ice sublimation conditions.

technology_to_test: GPS-denied SLAM LiDAR drone navigation in dark dusty caves
why_suitable: Rich volcanic lava tube, pit crater, and basaltic surface terrain supporting autonomous cave-entry robotics trials.
analogy_limitations: Atmospheric air enables rotorcraft lift (whereas lunar missions require thruster hoppers or climbing robots due to vacuum).

technology_to_test: Autonomous LiDAR drone, RF relay & lava-tube habitat module deployment
why_suitable: Intact natural basaltic lava tube with a solid ceiling, enabling GPS-denied 3D mapping and radiation-shielding evaluations.
analogy_limitations: Earth gravity (1g) far exceeds 0.165g on the Moon and 0.38g on Mars; interior contains humidity and convective air.

technology_to_test: Low-light LiDAR sensors, through-rock comms & cave-wall climbing robots
why_suitable: Large subterranean cavern volume suited for testing autonomous navigation in non-line-of-sight, pitch-dark environments.
analogy_limitations: Lithology is carbonate karst limestone rather than basaltic lava tubes, with dripping water and 1 atm air pressure.

technology_to_test: Dark-cave SLAM localization & underground wireless mesh relay
why_suitable: Complex multi-branching subterranean passages ideal for validating path-planning algorithms and RF attenuation in deep caves.
analogy_limitations: Humid limestone bedrock differs substantially from dry vacuum conditions and electrostatic dust in lunar pits.

technology_to_test: Skylight rappel tether robots & vertical shaft survey drones
why_suitable: Vertical sinkhole shaft geometry closely resembles lava-tube skylight openings, ideal for testing winch anchoring and vertical payload lowering.
analogy_limitations: Sinkhole floor holds liquid water and dense tropical vegetation, lacking vacuum and sharp abrasive regolith.

technology_to_test: Hyper-arid soil drills, biosignature sensors & evaporite salt analyzers
why_suitable: Classic hyper-arid environment with evaporite salt deposits and high UV flux closely matching Martian surface chemistry.
analogy_limitations: Surface temperatures are substantially warmer than Mars (-63°C mean) with a 1 atm O2/N2 atmosphere.

technology_to_test: Hydrothermal sensors, silica/sulfur biosignature detection & mineral coring
why_suitable: High-altitude geothermal spring field rich in silica/volcanic ash deposits analogous to ancient Martian hydrothermal sites (e.g., Home Plate).
analogy_limitations: Earth atmospheric pressure far exceeds Mars' ~6 mbar, allowing liquid water to remain stable at the surface.

technology_to_test: Permafrost core drilling & ground-penetrating radar (GPR)
why_suitable: Exposed permafrost megaslump with intense thermokarst degradation, ideal for testing ice-core drills and water-extraction sensors for polar/mid-latitude Mars.
analogy_limitations: Experiences summer thaw cycles (+25°C) and subarctic vegetation rather than lunar vacuum or Martian CO2 ice.

technology_to_test: Steep ash/basalt slope rover suspension & slip-resistant wheels
why_suitable: Steep volcanic slopes covered in loose volcanic ash and basalt, challenging rover traction and center-of-mass stability.
analogy_limitations: Humid clouds and active 1g atmospheric volcanism differ from airless vacuum regolith on the Moon.

technology_to_test: Evaporite salt spectroscopy, hard-crust drilling & high-albedo localization
why_suitable: Vast, hyper-arid, high-albedo evaporite salt flat suited for mineral spectrometer calibration and hydrated-salt extraction.
analogy_limitations: Broad flat surface floods seasonally and lacks the basalt-silicate composition dominant in lunar highlands.

technology_to_test: Rover traversal over fresh basalt (pahoehoe/a'a) & rough-terrain navigation
why_suitable: Iron- and magnesium-rich volcanic basalt closely matching lunar Mare plains and Martian volcanic lowlands.
analogy_limitations: Humid tropical atmosphere accelerates chemical weathering and lacks sharp micrometeorite-generated regolith dust.

technology_to_test: Large basaltic caldera traversal & high-resolution terrain mapping
why_suitable: Rugged basaltic caldera with layered lava flows supporting autonomous obstacle-avoidance evaluation.
analogy_limitations: Located in a humid equatorial zone with outer-slope vegetation and far milder temperatures than the Moon or Mars.

technology_to_test: Wheeled mobility on desert sand/sandstone & visual-inertial navigation
why_suitable: Arid desert valley with steep sandstone cliffs, ideal for Curiosity/Perseverance-style sand-trap avoidance testing.
analogy_limitations: 1g gravity alters soil compaction relative to 0.38g Mars; mineralogy is quartz-rich silicate rather than basalt-dominated.

technology_to_test: GNSS-denied narrow-canyon rover/drone navigation & cliff-wall LiDAR
why_suitable: Narrow slot canyon with steep walls causing multipath interference and sky occlusion, simulating rille or fracture navigation.
analogy_limitations: Sandstone formed by terrestrial flash-flood erosion rather than lava channels or impact fracturing.

technology_to_test: Ancient impact structure survey & shock-metamorphosed rock sampling
why_suitable: Largest verified impact structure on Earth, providing shock-metamorphosed rock samples analogous to lunar crater rims.
analogy_limitations: Heavily weathered over billions of years with modern vegetation and agricultural soil cover.

technology_to_test: High-altitude lava cavity robots & rough-surface RF communications
why_suitable: Multi-level basaltic lava tube system on an active volcano, well suited for testing planetary volcanic stratigraphy robots.
analogy_limitations: Geothermal/volcanic gas activity and temperate air differ from cryogenic vacuum inside lunar lava tubes.

technology_to_test: Basalt-andesite scoria slope rover climbing & altitude thermal-swing tests
why_suitable: Uniformly steep volcanic cone covered in loose scoria, enabling rover motor power-draw measurements during sustained ascents.
analogy_limitations: Seasonal wet snow and 1 atm air dissipate motor heat far more effectively than lunar vacuum.
